summary: @servicetitan/titan-chat-ui-common 9.0.7 ships preinstall dropper that fetches Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: package.json for this React chat UI library declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime (bun-v1.3.13) from GitHub releases, extracts it to a temporary directory, chmod +x's the binary, and invokes the sibling file math_init.js under Bun via execFileSync. math_init.js is a ~727 KB Bun-CJS bundle using string-array rotation obfuscation (WV8StW rotator, large mixed constants array, `_0x`-style identifiers). The package's declared purpose is `Chat experience UI package common files` with a React UI at dist/index.js; setup.mjs and math_init.js are unrelated to that dist tree and are auto-invoked on npm install. Fetching an alternate language runtime specifically to execute a heavily obfuscated bundled payload during a lifecycle hook is an alternate-runtime dropper pattern that evades Node-only inspection, and the mismatch between the package's advertised chat-UI purpose and the shipped install-time payload is consistent with a hijacked publish injecting a dropper into a legitimate ServiceTitan package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
